title: Tighten the invariant gates
summary: Closes the review findings against the commit and merge gates the invariant-foundations delivery landed: the commit hook reads a command the way git does, reads git as bytes under one shared deadline, and delivers every warning where the session can see it; the invariant register is held to an exact grammar, with every script an enforced or partial entry names verified; the register gate judges the register, carrier and script bytes the commit records, per commit shape; and git -C is accepted for this repository's own worktrees, with the landing gate judging the tree the merge targets. Every affected register entry, backlog item, and doctrine sentence flips in the same diff.
motivation: The landing review of karta/invariant-foundations/integration (tip 3b44ddc) confirmed nine findings against the delivered gates; a second planning run settled the deltas, and the reviews of this plan — the roundtable rounds the ledger beside this binder records, each with its provider tally and every finding's disposition, and the multi-lens panels, all against the branch source — reshaped it: the index-versus-worktree divergence denial became a recorded-bytes register check with two-phase materialization, the git -C rules became one consistent rule per hook, and the warn-and-allow outcomes gained a channel the session can see. This binder carries `after: ["invariant-foundations"]` because every item edits files only that branch delivers — two of them (scripts/check_invariant_register.py, scripts/hooks/_worktree.py) do not exist on main until it lands — so the status engine reads this binder as not-next until the landing, and the edge resolves against the archived predecessor as satisfied afterwards. It is committed only after the human has landed that branch. Decisions of record, cited by tag below: D1(h) — the landing-review finding that a -C merge naming the primary checkout, issued from a feature worktree with review disabled, passes the landing gate; D2 — the three findings the landing review rated plausible become properties with named cases that fail whenever the property is false; D4 — script tokens are verified on any bullet of an enforced or partial entry and never on a prose entry; D5 — the per-gate timeouts (20 s register checker, 90 s others) and the 600 s hook timeouts stay, and the shared deadline wraps them; D6 — AGENTS.md's Before-you-commit block stays at six commands; D7 — the register grammar line lives in exactly two places, the register's layer-2 paragraph and the checker docstring; D8 — INV-25 stays prose, with its script named as its own Carriers segment; D9 (revised on review) — the checker keeps reading a tree and the hook hands it the bytes the commit records; D11 — the INV-17 route gate is its own later binder.

work_items.title: The commit hook reads a commit command the way git reads it, and says its warnings where they are read
work_items.summary: Fix four ways the commit hook misreads a command or a git result, read a chained add the way the shell runs it, and give every warn-and-allow outcome one emitter the session can see, so the binder step runs on the commit git will actually make and every skip or plumbing failure is said where it is read instead of passing in silence.

contract.problem: scripts/hooks/precommit_gate.py (on the branch, 3b44ddc): _parse_commit_shape at :440-448 treats every letter of a short cluster as a flag, so `-mship` marks the shape opaque (the step is skipped) and `-ma` is read as --all; _token_segments at :335-359 tokenizes with shlex before splitting on operators, so `x.json&&git commit -m x` yields one glued token, commit_plan at :515 returns None, and the binder step is skipped with no message while is_commit_command's regex still runs the gate suite — and the split discards which operator joined the segments, so commit_plan (:531-538) counts an add joined by `;`, `||`, `|` or `&` as if the commit depended on it; _resolve_spec at :398 uses posixpath.isabs, which reads a Windows drive-letter path as relative; _name_status at :542-548 and _nul_paths at :569-573 return [] on a nonzero git result, so a failed enumeration looks like an empty one. And main() at :1679-1682 prints every message to stderr, which for an exit-0 outcome Claude Code routes to its debug log only — its hooks reference (read 2026-09-06): 'Stderr from a hook that exits 0 goes to the debug log only, never the transcript, and Claude never sees it' — while hook_main's internal-error path (:1012-1014) prints its own stderr line and returns an empty message; so every warning this hook has ever printed reached no one.
contract.attached_values: In a short cluster after `git commit`, the first letter that takes a value (the set the parser already holds for m, C, c, F, t) consumes the rest of that token as its value when any characters follow it, else the next token; letters after it are its value, never flags. `-mship` is a plain commit with message ship; `-ma` is a plain commit with message a and is not --all; `-am x` and `-a -m x` keep their meaning. A value-taking letter with nothing after it and no next token (`git commit -m`) is the usage error git raises: the shape is opaque and the named-skip warning says so. The short-letter set is named — git commit's own short options, a superset of the narrower whitelist roundtable_gate.py holds (:234-246 on the branch), which keeps denying the rest by name: a, i and o carry the shape of their long forms (--all, --include, --only: `-o --allow-empty -m x` records HEAD's tree with the index ignored and a bare `-o` is refused the way a bare --include is, both verified 2026-09-07); s, v, q, n, e and z are shape-free flags; p makes the shape opaque (--patch); m, C, c, F, t take a value; S and u take an optional attached value — the rest of the token is the value and the next token is never consumed (the seventeen short options `git commit -h` lists, checked 2026-09-07); any other letter makes the shape opaque and named-skipped, never a silent flag. The long-option set is named the same way: the long options `git commit -h` lists on the floor host, each boolean one with its --no- negation — the shape-bearing ones are --all, --include, --only, --amend, --dry-run, --allow-empty (which makes a bare --only legal), --fixup with a reword: value (which implies --only, where --fixup=amend: and a bare commit value record the index as any plain commit does, both verified 2026-09-07), --patch, --interactive and --pathspec-from-file (with --pathspec-file-nul), the last three opaque; the value-taking ones (--message, --reuse-message, --reedit-message, --file, --author, --date, --template, --fixup, --squash, --cleanup, --trailer, --pathspec-from-file) consume the next token or an =value; --untracked-files and --gpg-sign take an optional =value only; every other listed option (--no-verify, --signoff, --edit and --no-edit, --reset-author, --quiet, --verbose, --status, --short, --branch, --porcelain, --long, --null, --ahead-behind, --no-post-rewrite, --allow-empty-message, and their negations) is a plain flag. A --no- form cancels its option's state in token order, last wins, and the shape is derived from the options left standing: `--all --no-all` records the index, `--include --no-include -- <path>` is a pathspec commit, `--amend --no-amend` is a plain new commit (all verified 2026-09-07). An unrecognised long option makes the shape opaque and named-skipped: git accepts any unambiguous abbreviation (`--incl <path>` acts as --include, verified 2026-09-06), the hook implements no abbreviation table, and the branch silently ignores an unknown long option (:423-439), so `--incl` would be misread as a pathspec commit. A global -C before the verb is left exactly as this item finds it; the worktree-relocation-acceptance item owns it. commit_reads_worktree (the release block's own reader, :806-844) applies the same cluster rule, so both readers of a short cluster agree — until the recorded-bytes item retires that reader for the per-path source.
contract.glued_operators: An operator (&&, ||, ;, |, a bare &) with no whitespace around it, outside quotes, is a segment boundary exactly as a spaced one is, and so is a newline (the tokenizer already splits on it, :131 and :339-341), which the tokenizer keeps as `;` — a command on the next line runs whether or not the previous one succeeded (`git add nonexistent` on one line and the commit on the next: the add fails and the commit runs, verified 2026-09-07), matched longest-first (&& before &, || before |); a & or | that belongs to a redirection glyph — right after an unquoted > or <, or a & followed by > (2>&1, >&2, &>, <&) — is not a boundary, the rule roundtable_gate.py already applies at :276-300; `|&`, bash's pipe of both streams, is a pipe boundary exactly like `|`; a quoted operator inside a message stays text; a `--` ends option parsing and every later token is a pathspec. The tokenizer keeps the operator on each edge instead of discarding it. A chained add counts toward the commit's recorded bytes only when every operator from the add through the commit is `&&` — the one operator that makes each later segment depend on the earlier having succeeded; one rule, stated once: the add counts when every operator between it and the commit is `&&`, and an operator earlier in the chain that leaves the add conditional (a `||` before it) drops it too — with a `;`, `|`, `&` or a newline between the add and the commit, or a `||` before the add, the add may not have run, or may have failed, when the commit runs (`true || git add x && git commit` skips the add and runs the commit, verified 2026-09-06), so the ADD's contribution is dropped rather than the whole commit: the commit's own shape still decides its recorded bytes, the index-sourced candidates are still enumerated and still validated, and the warning names the dropped add by its own arguments as written on the command line — not the paths they would expand to, which `git add .` and `git add -A` do not enumerate without a filesystem walk the hook never makes. Dropping the whole shape would lose denials the branch delivers today — measured 2026-09-07 against the branch, both `echo hi; git add <binder> && git commit -m y` and `git commit -m a && git commit -m b` return an index candidate and can deny an invalid staged binder — and a fix that trades an existing denial for a warning is a regression, not a tightening. A payload holding more than one true commit is read the same way: the first commit's shape is judged, its candidates enumerated and validated, and every later commit is named in the warning as a subsequent commit this run did not judge — not as an add, which it is not. A segment before the commit that is not a git add is a mutator the hook cannot see; the recorded-bytes item states what the register gate does with it. `git add x.json&&git commit -m x` is the add-then-commit chain and the step validates the working-tree bytes the add covers.
contract.add_modes: An add's options decide what it stages, and the parser models them or goes opaque: -u/--update covers tracked paths only (the exception the hook already states, :261-263); -A/--all and a bare pathspec cover untracked paths too; -N/--intent-to-add records nothing for its paths under a plain commit (verified in a clean repository 2026-09-07: the commit succeeds with the path absent from its tree; a pathspec naming the path, or -a, records its working-tree bytes), and it, --ignore-removal, --renormalize, --chmod and any add option the parser does not model make the shape opaque and named-skipped.
contract.named_skip: Whenever a true commit is detected and the binder step does not run — an opaque shape (--patch, --interactive, --pathspec-from-file, a glob or magic pathspec on the commit, a bare value-taking option, an unknown short letter, an unrecognised long option, an add option the parser does not model, a pathspec-mode global before the verb — --literal-pathspecs, --glob-pathspecs, --noglob-pathspecs, --icase-pathspecs, which the branch accepts as inert flags at :297-298 although `git --icase-pathspecs commit -- agents.md` records AGENTS.md (verified 2026-09-07) — a -c or --config-env global whose key begins with core. or filter. on a shape that reads the working tree (-a, a pathspec, --include, or a chained add) — over-defense within those shapes, since most keys under those prefixes cannot change recorded bytes and the cost of naming them there is a warning; on a plain commit and on --amend --only the recorded bytes are index or HEAD blobs no clean filter touches (verified 2026-09-07: a plain commit with CRLF already in the index records those bytes byte-identically under -c core.autocrlf=input), so the shape stays readable and its denial is kept rather than traded for a warning — which can change the bytes git records from a working-tree path (`git -c core.autocrlf=input commit -- <path>` records LF where the disk holds CRLF and the index copy holds none, and records CRLF where the index copy already holds it — git skips the conversion then — both verified 2026-09-07, and either way the flag can change the recorded bytes; any other key stays inert, as the branch treats every -c at :293), and a commit that does not head its segment after any VAR=value prefix — a wrapper such as env, time or sudo before git, which is_true_commit sees (:146-149) while the anchored parser does not, so the branch passes it over silently, or quoting the tokenizer cannot parse — the hook emits one warning naming which shape it could not read; a dry run is not in that set, since --dry-run is modelled (:429-430) and records nothing, so it is passed over without a warning, which is what row 8 of the recorded-bytes item already says, and shape-skip-is-named carries the positive control that makes the silence discriminating: `git commit --dry-run -m x` over an invalid staged binder exits 0 with nothing on either stream. That arm is required rather than decorative, because the branch collapses the two paths identically at :529 (`if shape.dry_run or shape.opaque: return None`) — this item is newly splitting behaviours that are byte-identical today, so an implementation that warns on a dry run passes every other case. Through the warning channel, exit 0. A payload holding more than one true commit is not one of these opaque shapes: the first commit's shape is judged, its candidates enumerated and validated, and it can still deny — the branch's commit_plan reads the first only (:520-523), so the hook additionally warns naming the later commit this run did not judge, which is what glued_operators, shape-skip-is-named and the recorded-bytes item's row 8 already say. A directory pathspec on the commit (a trailing slash, a directory name, `.`) is a resolvable containment, not a glob: the shape stays readable, and the recorded-bytes item states what it covers. Every skip is named except one class: a relocating global (the _GIT_RELOCATING set at :299 — -C, --git-dir, --work-tree, --namespace, --super-prefix) keeps the named residual the NAMED RESIDUAL BOUNDS comment and INV-7 state, worded for the whole set, until the worktree-relocation-acceptance item rescopes -C and names the redirect residual; the delivery lands whole, so no tree on main carries this item's claim without that rescoping.
contract.warning_channel: The hook has exactly one output site: main() calls emit_outcome(code, message). For exit 0 with a message it writes one JSON object to stdout carrying the message twice — as systemMessage, the field the Claude Code hooks reference (raw page, read 2026-09-06) defines as 'Warning message shown to the user' and names as the way 'To surface a message to the user on any platform', and as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext with hookEventName PreToolUse, the field the same reference defines for PreToolUse as 'String added to Claude's context alongside the tool result' — so the person and the worker both read it. The pairing is required rather than redundant: a PreToolUse hook returning systemMessage with no hookSpecificOutput beside it has it silently dropped, shown to no one and added to no context (anthropics/claude-code#40380, read 2026-09-07), so a warning that carried only the first field would not arrive at all. The same reference caps additionalContext, systemMessage and plain stdout at 10,000 characters, saving the overflow to a file and passing a preview and a path instead, so emit_outcome caps its joined message the way TAIL_LINES already caps a deny reason — a commit that trips several gate warnings at once must still deliver a message where this item promises one. The same text goes to stderr for the debug log. For exit 0 with no message it writes nothing; for exit 2 it writes the reason to stderr only, which the reference routes to Claude as the blocking message ('A hook that blocks by exiting 2 routes the same way as "deny": Claude sees the stderr message as the denial reason'). The object carries no permissionDecision, so the normal permission flow applies, exactly as the reference describes for exit 0 with no decision, and the oracle asserts that literal is absent from the hook — because the workaround offered for an invisible warning is to add `permissionDecision: 'allow'`, which on PreToolUse decides the tool call instead of annotating it: it would turn this warn-and-allow emitter into one that approves every commit it warns about and skips the permission flow that would otherwise ask. A gate that warns must not be the thing that grants. hook_main's internal-error path returns its warning through hook_main's own (code, message) result instead of printing it, so an internal error is named in the transcript too, and every warn-and-allow outcome of every item — the named skip, a plumbing failure, an exhausted budget or deadline, an unjudged relocation — reaches the session through emit_outcome; no path prints a bare stderr line for an exit-0 outcome. The same gate runs under Codex through scripts/hooks/codex_precommit_gate.py (wired in .codex/hooks.json), whose delegate call (branch :63-67) runs the gate without capturing its stdout, so the line reaches Codex unchanged and no adapter edit is needed. What Codex does with it is checked rather than disclaimed (developers.openai.com/codex/hooks and codex-rs/hooks/src/events/pre_tool_use.rs, read 2026-09-07): on exit 0 Codex parses a PreToolUse hook's stdout, surfaces systemMessage as a warning and appends hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext as model-visible context, so both halves of this object are supported and consumed there. The constraint that comes with it is a build rule: the object carries systemMessage and hookSpecificOutput only, never continue, stopReason or suppressOutput — Codex marks a PreToolUse hook that returns any of those as failed and reports the error (it continues the tool call), which is a shipped failure in the wild for a Claude-Code-shaped emitter that always set suppressOutput. Plain non-JSON stdout is ignored on both hosts; JSON-looking stdout that does not parse is a reported failure, which is why the emitter writes one object or nothing. One check the self-test cannot make is made by hand, and not inside this delivery: while the items are built and verified, the session's hook is main's copy (.claude/settings.json runs the primary checkout's scripts/hooks/precommit_gate.py through CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR — the verify-doctrine gap this binder's scope names), so a named skip triggered then never runs the edited emitter. The check runs after landing, on the primary checkout, by the person who landed it: trigger a named skip (a --patch commit is enough) in a live Claude Code session and confirm the warning is shown and that the worker's next turn can see it — or earlier, in a session started with the item worktree as its project directory. The build notes record only that the JSON shape is pinned by warning-channel-system-message; they claim no live observation.
contract.windows_absolute: _resolve_spec recognises an absolute path on either convention (a leading slash, or a drive letter followed by a colon with either separator) by rule, before any join: a spelling the host's os.path.isabs accepts is resolved against the root through realpath; a drive-letter spelling the host does not accept (POSIX) is None — outside the repository — without being handed to realpath, which would join it onto the process cwd (verified 2026-09-07: realpath of C:/x on this host is the cwd plus C:/x, and os.path.isabs rejects it). A drive-letter path is never joined onto the cwd prefix as if it were relative; on a POSIX host it makes the shape opaque, which the named-skip warning then reports.
contract.plumbing_warns: _name_status and _nul_paths each return their pairs plus a failure note when git exits nonzero; binder_candidates and binder_block carry that note into the warning channel, so a commit whose enumeration failed is allowed with a warning naming the plumbing command and its exit code — never silently treated as recording no binder. Both helpers are proven separately: `diff --cached --name-status -z` failing exercises _name_status, `ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z` failing exercises _nul_paths.
contract.cases: Twelve new self-test cases, each id the first word of its check() message so it prints on its [PASS] line, and each case one check() call — a case with several arms reports the first arm that fails in its message, so its id appears on exactly one status line per run, which passed() in every oracle here requires: shape-attached-short-value (an invalid staged binder is denied under `-mship`), shape-attached-short-value-not-all (a modified-but-unstaged binder is not a candidate under `-ma`, and the per-path source is the index for it; `-o --allow-empty -m x` over a staged binder judges HEAD's bytes, not the index — red on the branch, which models only a, i and p (:441-447) — and a bare `-o` is the refusal git raises, so the shape is opaque and named-skipped; `-s -m x` with an invalid staged binder is a plain commit and is denied; `-Sabc -m x` is plain and not --all), shape-glued-operator-splits (`git add x.json&&git commit -m x` splits at the operator and the add counts; `cmd 2>&1 && git add x && git commit -m y` counts x's working-tree bytes, the redirection glyph being no boundary), shape-chain-edge-semantics (`git add x && git commit` counts x's working-tree bytes; the same add joined by `;`, `|`, `|&`, `&` and a newline, and `true || git add x && git commit`, drop the add's contribution and keep the commit — the discriminating arm, red under both the branch's reading and the whole-shape skip: with an invalid binder already staged, `git add other; git commit -m x` is still denied with exit 2, and the warning names the dropped add's arguments and nothing else), shape-add-modes (under `git add -u . && git commit` an untracked binder is not a candidate; `git add -N x && git commit` is opaque with the named skip), shape-skip-is-named (the warning carries the skip for `--patch`, for an unparseable command, for a bare `-m`, for an unknown short letter, for `--incl`, for --icase-pathspecs before the verb, for -c core.autocrlf=input before the verb, and, for `git commit -m a && git commit -m b`, a warning naming the subsequent commit while the first commit is still judged — an invalid staged binder is denied with exit 2 there, not allowed; the positive controls are a plain commit, `git -c core.autocrlf=input commit -m x` over an invalid staged binder — still denied exit 2 and unwarned, because the narrowing keeps the skip to working-tree-reading shapes; work_items.title: The invariant register is held to a strict grammar, and every script an enforced or partial entry names is verified
work_items.summary: Replace the register checker's tolerant reading of a carriers line with one exact grammar, state one rule for what counts as a script token on a prose bullet, verify every script path an enforced or partial entry names on any of its bullets, rewrite the register entries that leaned on the old tolerance, and correct the doctrine sentences that overstate what the commit gate does.

contract.problem: scripts/check_invariant_register.py (branch): split_segments at :172-196 passes an unterminated quote and an unbalanced parenthesis silently; an empty `- Carriers:` value produces no segments and no failure (:263-275); _carrier_and_scripts at :209-220 accepts free prose beside a file token; _SCRIPT_RE at :111 recognises script tokens only under scripts/, skills/, benchmarks/; scripts are collected from the Carriers bullet alone (:259-263, :275-276) and verified only there (:301-307); carrier files are decoded with errors=replace at :248, so an undecodable carrier can pass its phrase check. Five register entries rely on the prose tolerance today: INV-3 (:85), INV-5 (:99), INV-11 (:135), INV-16 (:162), INV-25 (:213); INV-19's status bullet (:180) names four scripts by bare basename; INV-8's Carriers bullet (:118) follows `none yet` with a clause.
contract.grammar: A Carriers value is a sequence of segments separated by `; ` outside quotes and parentheses, optionally followed by one sentence-final `.` (the register's bullets are sentences: the period is permitted after the last segment and ignored, and nothing else may follow it). On an entry whose status is prose or prose by design only, the value may instead be exactly `none yet` (plus that optional period); any text after it is a named parse failure, and `none yet` on an enforced or partial entry is one too. A segment is exactly `file ["label"] [("phrase" [; "phrase"])]`: one repo-relative file token ending .md or .py (bare or in backticks, no leading slash, no `..`), then an optional double-quoted label, then an optional parenthesised list of double-quoted phrases separated by `; `. Every double-quoted string in the segment — the label and each phrase — must be present in that file, whitespace-normalized and case-sensitive, as today. Anything else beside the file token — unquoted words, a second file token, unquoted text inside the parentheses — is a named parse failure citing the entry id, the line, and the offending segment. An empty Carriers value, an unterminated quote, and an unbalanced parenthesis are each a named parse failure by their own name. The grammar line `file ["label"] [("phrase" [; "phrase"])]` appears verbatim in exactly two places in the repository: the register's layer-2 paragraph (docs/conventions/invariants.md, 'How this file stays true', item 2) and the checker's module docstring; docs/backlog/README.md item 21 points at those two and states no grammar of its own (decision D7), and the oracle proves the two-places rule repo-wide, excluding only .karta/ (binders and review records quote the line), .worktrees/ and node_modules/.
contract.scripts: A script token is found in one order: double-quoted phrases are masked wherever the checker takes tokens — every segment and every bullet, not the Carriers segment alone (a path inside a quoted phrase or label is text, never a token — the masking rule below), link syntax and backticks are removed, and every maximal run of the characters [A-Za-z0-9_./-] — not preceded by one of them and not followed by a letter, digit, underscore or hyphen, the branch's _TOKEN_RE at :109-110 — is taken; trailing period and hyphen characters are stripped from the run (the only characters of the set that can end one — a comma, semicolon, colon, closing parenthesis or quote cannot occur inside a run and so ends it by construction); what remains is a script token when it ends in .py and starts with an alphanumeric character or a dot — a .py under a dot-directory such as .codex-plugin/ is a token, as the carrier grammar already admits .karta/ paths — (a run preceded by a colon or a slash, as in a URL, is not a token; a run carrying its own leading slash that no colon or slash precedes — `/scripts/x.py` — is a named parse failure on an enforced or partial entry, telling the author to write the repo-relative path, exactly like the bare basename). A following argument such as `--check` is a separate run, never part of the token; a run that is not a script token after this rule is prose, silently, on every entry, except as the next sentence names. On an enforced or partial entry, a whitespace-delimited word of the masked segment that ends in .py after the same stripping and contains a glob metacharacter (*, ?, [) — checked on the word before the character-set run is taken, since the run itself cannot hold those characters — or a run with a `..` segment, is a named parse failure — it can never resolve to a file — rather than a silent non-token; on a prose entry it is ignored like every other token there. For an entry whose status is enforced or partial, every script token on ANY of its bullets (status, Carriers, or a note) must exist as a repo-relative path under --root, wherever in the tree it lives — the three-directory restriction goes. A script token with no directory component (a bare basename) on such an entry is a named parse failure telling the author to write the repo-relative path. Entries whose status is prose or prose by design are never script-verified, and the checker docstring's 'SCRIPT SCOPE, narrowed deliberately' paragraph is replaced by this rule (decision D4). A script token that is a segment's sole file token is that segment's carrier, as today, so a prose entry's carrier script is still existence-checked by the carrier rule (INV-25). precommit_gate.py's self-test spawns the register gate as a stubbed command and, on the branch, writes no register fixture (verified 2026-09-06: the branch file contains no Carriers or '### INV' text), so the stricter grammar cannot change its count at this item's point; the oracle's precommit floor is a regression guard only. The recorded-bytes item later adds fixture registers to that self-test, written under this grammar.

work_items.title: The register gate judges the register, carrier and script bytes the commit records
work_items.summary: Close the gap between what the register checker reads and what the commit records: for every commit shape the hook can read, the register is materialized as the bytes that shape records, the paths it names are listed from that copy and materialized the same way, and the checker runs on that tree — so a partial staging can no longer commit a register or carrier the gate never saw, without a single denial of an honest commit that records what passed.

contract.problem: The register checker reads the working tree of the resolved root (scripts/check_invariant_register.py docstring :20-22; register layer-2 paragraph :53-55; INV-20 :185; backlog item 21 :534-538 all name this as an open bound), so a partial staging can commit register or carrier bytes the checker never saw. The first plan for this item — deny when the index and the working tree differ — was withdrawn on review (2026-09-06): index-versus-worktree is what a plain commit records, but a pathspec commit records HEAD's bytes for a path the pathspec does not name and -a records the working tree, so the divergence rule would have passed the one drift it existed to catch and denied honest -a and pathspec commits, and it would have blocked every unrelated commit while a carrier held unstaged work. A second review (round 2) corrected the first recorded-bytes draft: the carrier list must come from the recorded register, not the working copy; a parse failure in the recorded register is a verdict, not a plumbing failure; the temporary root must hold the script files the strict checker stats; and --include records index bytes, not HEAD's, for the paths it does not name. Decision D9, revised: the checker keeps reading a tree; the hook hands it the bytes the commit records.
contract.listing: scripts/check_invariant_register.py gains `--list-inputs`: with --root it parses the register under the strict grammar and prints, one repo-relative path per line, every filesystem path the checker would read or stat under that root — the register path first, then every carrier file token and every script token it verifies (the script tokens of enforced and partial entries, the grammar item's rule), each once, sorted; exit 0. --list-inputs parses and prints only: it reads the register and nothing else, and reads or stats no listed path, so it runs on a root holding only the register. A parse failure prints the failures and exits 1 exactly as the plain run does; a register missing or unreadable under --root exits 1 the same way; a crash exits 2. The checker also gains `--register-path`, which prints the register's repo-relative path — the one constant the checker already holds — and exits 0 without reading anything, so phase one below asks the checker where the register lives and the hook carries no copy of that location. One parser: the hook never re-derives carriers or scripts with a regex of its own, and the hook's code above its self-test (the part before `def _run_self_test`) contains no `Carriers:` literal — the self-test itself writes fixture registers, which carry the bullet by necessity.
contract.recorded_bytes: For a true commit whose shape commit_plan can read, the register gate runs on the bytes that shape records, in two phases. Phase one: the hook takes the register's own recorded bytes for that shape, writes them under a temporary root at the register's path, and runs the checker there with --list-inputs; a listing exit 1 is the checker's verdict on the recorded register — a parse failure in what the commit records — and the gate denies with that output. Phase two: for every listed path the hook takes the bytes this commit records, writes them under the same root at their repo-relative paths, and runs the checker there with --root; its exit is the gate's verdict. The byte source per shape is one table — the WHAT BYTES rule the binder step already applies (:254-266) — written out row by row so a missing row is visible, each row reproduced in a scratch repository on 2026-09-06 and 2026-09-07: (1) a plain commit records the index blob of every path; (2) a pathspec commit (--only, the default when pathspecs are given) records working-tree bytes for a covered path git knows (in the index or in HEAD — a path removed with rm --cached but present on disk is recorded from disk), absence for a covered known path deleted on disk, and HEAD's blob for an uncovered path; a listed path is covered exactly when it equals the normalized spec or begins with the normalized spec followed by a slash — `.` normalizes to the empty spec and covers everything, a trailing slash is dropped by the normalization _resolve_spec already applies (:398), and `docs` does not cover docs-other/x — and a covered path git does not know is absent from the recorded tree: git refuses the command when a spec matches nothing it knows ('did not match any file(s) known to git') and proceeds when a directory spec matches a known sibling, recording no untracked path under it (both verified 2026-09-07), so the hook judges the absence and does not predict the refusal — the verdict on that carrier is the same either way; with no HEAD to read (an unborn branch) an uncovered listed path is absent without a read, since a pathspec commit on an unborn branch records only its covered paths (verified 2026-09-07), and phase one, finding no register bytes, denies with the checker's missing-register verdict; (3) --include records working-tree bytes for a covered path the index holds and the index blob for an uncovered path, under the same coverage rule; known here means in the index — a covered path only in HEAD (rm --cached, still on disk) is absent from the recorded tree exactly as an untracked one is: git refuses an exact spec matching nothing in the index and proceeds for a directory spec with an indexed sibling, recording the path as deleted (`--include` probes 2026-09-07); (4) -a records working-tree bytes for a tracked path present on disk, absence for a tracked path deleted on disk, and nothing for an untracked path — tracked here means in the index, as in row 3, not in HEAD: a path added to the index and then modified on disk is recorded from disk under -a although HEAD has never held it (verified 2026-09-07, where the same path under a plain commit records its index blob); (5) a chained add — every operator before the commit `&&`, every add option one the parser models; a newline between the add and the commit is not `&&` — composes: the add places working-tree bytes into the index for the paths it covers (untracked included, except under -u), and then the commit's own row applies to that index, so a plain commit and --include record those bytes while a pathspec commit records them only for a path the pathspec also covers and HEAD's blob otherwise (`git add car && git commit -- oth` records HEAD's car); (6) --amend builds the same tree as its underlying shape and only changes the parent; --only, or its short spelling -o, with no pathspec — legal beside --amend, beside --allow-empty, or as --fixup=reword, since git refuses it alone ('No paths with --include/--only does not make sense'); --fixup=reword implies it — records HEAD's blob for every path with the index ignored (`--only --allow-empty` and `--fixup=reword:HEAD` over a staged change, both verified 2026-09-07), so the parser keeps an explicit --only or -o as state where the branch drops it (:433-434); --amend with a pathspec follows row 2 for its paths — covered from the working tree, uncovered from HEAD (verified 2026-09-07); (6b) a modelled, resolvable add joined to the commit by anything but `&&` — `git add car; git commit -m x` and the newline spelling — takes the commit's own row for every path, with the add-covered paths judged from the index the commit records rather than from disk, since whether the add ran is not decidable from the command text; the warning names those paths as unverified, and recorded-semi-joined-add-index-bytes is the arm that makes this row discriminating rather than decorative: `git add car; git commit -m x` where car's index copy lacks the phrase and its disk copy carries it is denied from the index bytes, with the warning naming car as unverified — red if a build routes the non-&&-joined add to row 5's post-add bytes or to row 7's working-tree run, which is the whole command class this row exists to place; (7) a chained add with a spec the parser cannot resolve (a glob, a magic pathspec), and any segment before the commit that is not a git add (a mutator the hook cannot see: `sed -i` on a carrier, then the add, then the commit), are opaque for the register gate: the working-tree run with the named-skip warning — commit_plan records the fact (an unresolved add spec, a non-add segment) on the plan it already returns, the register gate reads that flag, and the binder step is unchanged (it reads working-tree bytes for the paths the add covers, and a mutation after its read stays INV-7's named remainder, untouched here); the warning names the register gate. The working-tree run reads the tree the hook already judges, the payload cwd's root — so `cd <worktree> && git commit`, the shape karta-build prescribes to a worker whose harness resets the cwd between calls, is the cd chain INV-11 already names: it warns on every such commit, the warning saying which tree was judged, and docs/how-to/hooks.md points a worker in a linked worktree at `git -C <worktree> commit`, the shape the relocation item accepts and rescopes; (8) a dry run, an opaque shape, or a loose match that is not a true commit (commit-graph, commit-tree — the binder step's _TRUE_COMMIT_RE decides, so the loose regex never selects the recorded-bytes run) takes the working-tree run, as today, with the named-skip warning saying so for an opaque shape; (9) a redirected command (--git-dir, --work-tree, --namespace, a GIT_* prefix) has no recorded-bytes run at all — the relocation item names that residual. git itself refuses -a with a pathspec ('with -a does not make sense'), -a with --include, -a with --only in every spelling and --include with --only ('cannot be used together' — `-a -o --allow-empty`, `--amend -a -o` and `-a -o -- <path>` all refused, verified 2026-09-07), -a beside --fixup=reword ('reword option of --fixup and --patch/--interactive/--all/--include/--only cannot be used together', same date), and --include or --only with no pathspec unless --amend or --allow-empty stands beside --only ('No paths with --include/--only does not make sense' — a bare --include refuses even beside --allow-empty, verified 2026-09-07), so no row combines them and the hook treats such a command as opaque. Working-tree bytes are read from disk: the hook applies no clean filter, eol conversion or symlink resolution, and on this repository's carriers — LF text, a .gitattributes declaring `-text -filter` under .karta/ and nothing elsewhere, no symlinked carrier (verified 2026-09-06) — disk bytes are the blob bytes; INV-20 names that bound for whatever changes it — an attribute, a host setting, or a config prefix the hook does not read (GIT_CONFIG_*, GIT_ATTR_NOSYSTEM); a -c or --config-env global under core. or filter. is the commit-shape item's named skip instead. An intent-to-add entry reads from the index as the empty blob although a plain commit records no path for it (verified 2026-09-07); the hook does not tell the two apart, so a carrier or script still intent-to-add is judged as empty rather than absent — a named remainder in INV-20, never a claim. A path with no blob in the recorded tree is absent from the temporary root — an untracked carrier under rows 1 and 4, a tracked carrier deleted on disk under row 4, a script staged for deletion — and the checker names it; the register itself absent from the recorded tree (staged for deletion, or deleted on disk under -a) leaves phase one with no register bytes, so --list-inputs exits 1 with its missing-register verdict and the gate denies, remedy 'restore it (git restore --staged --worktree -- <path>)'. Index and HEAD blobs are read with one `git cat-file --batch` call each, the object names `:<path>` and `HEAD:<path>` fed on stdin (never as arguments, so the listing's size cannot become a plumbing failure), under the shared deadline. Absence is read from the stream, never from the exit code: the batch prints `<name> missing` for an object it does not have and still exits 0 — even when every requested object is missing, and for `HEAD:<path>` on an unborn branch (verified 2026-09-07 on git 2.47.3, and the documented contract rather than this host's behaviour: git-cat-file(1) states that a name given on stdin which cannot be resolved to an object makes cat-file ignore any custom format and print `<object> SP missing LF`, with no nonzero exit attached to it) — so a missing line is the absence rows 1 to 6 judge and only a nonzero exit is the plumbing failure that warns. The temporary root is created per judged commit and removed in a finally clause (shutil.rmtree, ignore_errors) around both phases, on every exit — deny, warn-and-allow, crash. The gate's output is prefixed with 'the register gate judged the bytes this commit records (<shape>)' and, for each failing path, the remedy for that shape: a plain commit — 'stage it (git add -- <path>) to record the bytes that pass, or restore the index copy'; a pathspec that leaves the path out — 'name it in the pathspec'; an untracked carrier — 'add it (git add -- <path>) or remove it from the register'; a tracked carrier deleted on disk (row 2 covered, row 4) — 'restore it (git restore --worktree -- <path>) or remove it from the register', since git add on a deleted path stages the deletion. One run per commit: on the recorded bytes for rows 1 to 6, on the working tree for rows 7 and 8; a payload holding more than one true commit is judged on its first commit, by that commit's own row, with the later commits named in the warning — the reading item 1 states, since sending the whole payload to the working-tree run would drop a denial the branch delivers. The release block's read of plugin.json goes through the same table: commit_reads_worktree (:806-844) reduces the whole commit to one boolean — working tree for -a or a pathspec, index otherwise — so `--include other` reads disk where git records the index, `git add plugin.json && git commit` reads the pre-add index where git records the post-add bytes, and `--amend --only` reads the index where git records HEAD, any of which can arm or disarm the version-bump check wrongly; it is retired, the release block takes plugin.json's source from the plan's per-path resolution, and an opaque shape keeps today's working-tree read. The same reader decides the block's evidence, so the evidence moves with it: the gate files are enumerated from disk with gate_dir.glob and parsed with p.read_text (:876-880), and one is called committed when `rel in staged or (worktree_mode and p.is_file())` (:905) — so under -a or a pathspec any green gate file merely present on disk counts as evidence although the commit records none of it (untracked under -a, or outside the pathspec), and a file green on disk but red in the index passes. Candidates under GATE_RESULTS_REL are discovered from the union of the working tree and the recorded tree — the disk walk stays, because the branch's own diagnostics depend on seeing a file it will then refuse: green-but-unstaged-gate-file-blocks and its 'run git add <gate>' remedy (:1173-1175) drive a gate file present on disk and absent from the index, and a recorded-tree-only enumeration never visits it, never sets seen['unstaged'], and takes both checks and the floor down with it. What changes is the verdict, not the search: each candidate's bytes come from the same per-path table, and committed means the recorded tree holds it and those bytes are green — a file seen only on disk is classified 'unstaged' and named, never counted. The query per row is stated with the table: the index listing for a plain commit (unchanged entries included, which `diff --cached` omits and which are evidence), HEAD's tree for --amend --only, the coverage-filtered union for a pathspec or --include, the post-add index for a chained add, and the disk walk alone for an opaque shape. work_items.title: git -C is accepted for this repository's own worktrees, and the landing gate judges the tree the merge targets
work_items.summary: Let both hooks accept a commit or merge that names one of this repository's worktrees with git -C and judge it on that worktree; the review gate denies a relocating landing it cannot resolve, and the commit hook allows an unresolvable relocation with a warning that nothing was judged — so the landing gate can no longer be passed by relocating the merge, and an agent can commit from a linked worktree it cannot make its working directory.

contract.problem: Backlog item 22 (:542-558): the review gate denies `git -C <path>` as a relocating prefix (roundtable_gate.py :83-84 in the grammar docstring, the Denial at :833-835, the suite at :1922-1927), and the commit hook skips its binder step for it (precommit_gate.py :526-527), while the agent harness resets every shell call's cwd to the primary checkout, so an agent has no accepted way to commit in a linked worktree. Finding D1(h): with review disabled, a -C merge naming the primary checkout and karta/x/integration, issued from a worktree on a feature branch, passes the landing gate, because decide() reads the cwd's branch (:1531-1538) and only the review grammar — which enabled:false switches off (:1571-1572) — denies the relocation; the same hole is reachable with --git-dir, --work-tree or a GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE prefix in place of -C.
contract.acceptance: A single `git -C <path>` global before `commit` or `merge` is resolved the same way in both hooks: <path>, joined to the payload cwd when relative and normalized with realpath (so `-C .` from a top and a symlinked spelling compare equal), is passed through scripts/hooks/_worktree.py's resolve_invocation_root, which answers the worktree top of this repository that contains it, or None. Every lookup — the landing gate's branch and default branch, the config in HEAD, the index, HEAD blobs, working-tree bytes, pathspec resolution — is rescoped to that top. A relative pathspec is resolved against the -C target directory, as git resolves it, and then normalized to a repo-relative path against that worktree's top — never against the payload cwd. Two -C options, -C combined with --git-dir/--work-tree/--namespace, a GIT_* prefix, a cd chain, and every other relocation stay denied by name in the review gate exactly as on the branch; a cwd-changing wrapper before git divides exactly as scope.excluded states it: xargs and a loop body stay what AGENTS.md's landing-gate section already names — uncaught by anchoring, never accepted — while a merge naming an integration ref whose leading wrapper chain carries an option that sets the directory git runs in — decided from what the gate's own wrapper parser resolves, never from a list of spellings, and read over the whole chain rather than its head — is denied by name under every switch. Detection is not rescoping, and the branch already detects: _head strips the wrapper, so the merge is seen. What it does not do is resolve the wrapper's target, so scope() reads the payload cwd's branch while git lands in the relocated tree. Measured 2026-09-07 on the landed tree (main at 6555869): with the review switch off, or with KARTA_SKIP_ROUNDTABLE=1 set, `env --chdir=<primary> git merge --no-ff --no-edit karta/x/integration` issued from a linked worktree returns exit 0, where the same command against the pre-landing gate returned exit 2. So this denial restores a block the worktree rescoping traded away, and it is red before this item builds — not a guard over behaviour that already holds. Acceptance covers commit and merge only: git pull, cherry-pick, rebase and reset --hard are not gated by either hook (the accepted-bypass family AGENTS.md names), so a -C before them is neither accepted nor denied — not covered, a residual INV-11 and the roundtable how-to name in those words. A -C value carrying an unexpanded ~, $, glob or brace character is not resolvable from text: the commit hook treats it as a redirected command (below) and the review gate denies it as today. A glued `-C<path>` is a git usage error, not a relocation (verified 2026-09-06); the `=`-joined --git-dir=, --work-tree= and --namespace= spellings are the same relocation as the spaced ones, as both hooks already parse them.
contract.review_gate: roundtable_gate.py accepts the -C when the resolved top equals the realpath of <path> — the top itself, not a subdirectory of it (the rule _check_cwd applies to a cwd) — and rescopes; a subdirectory is denied by name as today. The relocation is resolved BEFORE the landing gate compares branches: scope() takes the -C target into account, so a relocating merge is judged on the target tree's branch. A merge naming a karta/*/integration ref that carries any relocation other than a single -C resolving to a worktree top of this repository — an unresolvable -C, two -C options, --git-dir, --work-tree, --namespace, --super-prefix, or a redirecting environment prefix (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_NAMESPACE, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES, the four pathspec-mode names GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS, GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS, GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS and GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS, which change which paths a spec covers exactly as the flag spellings item 1 makes opaque do (verified 2026-09-07: `GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS=1 git commit -m x -- upper.md` records Upper.md, where the same spec without it is refused), and any name beginning GIT_CONFIG_ or GIT_ATTR_, which redirects the config or attributes that decide what git records from a working-tree path; the inert values the review gate already tolerates in its environment — INERT_GIT_ENV at :175, GIT_EDITOR=true, GIT_PAGER=cat and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 — relocate nothing and change nothing here, and as a command-text prefix the review gate keeps denying them by name, since ALLOWED_PREFIXES (:172) holds only the two KARTA_* assignments) — is denied outright, by name, before the skip hatch and before the config switch — with review enabled or disabled, with KARTA_SKIP_ROUNDTABLE=1, and with KARTA_LANDING_APPROVED=1 — because the gate cannot tell whether that merge is a landing of this repository, and a landing decision never depends on the review environment (INV-18) nor on the review hatch: this is deliberately the one denial no hatch passes, and the contract, AGENTS.md's landing-gate section and the roundtable how-to say so, with the remedy 'run the merge from that worktree'.
